newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Crack troops depart to protect Portuguese in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Crack troops depart to protect Portuguese in Zaire.

text.p: Two military planes left for the Congo on Tuesday carrying 68 crack troops and a medical team to protect Portuguese nationals if they have to be evacuated from the rebel-targeted capital of nearby Zaire, a senior official said.

Rebels opposing the rule of President Mobutu Sese Seko were closing in on Kinshasa. Some reports said the rebels led by Laurent Kabila were less than 85 km (50 miles) from the Zairean city of five million.

"Two C-130 military transport planes left for Brazzaville this afternoon. The soldiers' mission is strictly humanitarian. They will not intervene in the internal affairs of Zaire," said Jose Lello, Secretary of State for Portuguese Communities.

"The mission of the special forces soldiers will be to protect Portuguese citizens if they have to be evacuated from Kinshasa," Lello, who recently visited Kinshasa to help prepare the evacuation plan, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We hope that a peaceful, democratic solution can be reached in Zaire, without the use of arms," he added.

He said that if the situation deteriorated, some 400 Portuguese who live in Kinshasa, mainly businessmen and their families, would head for designated "welcome centres" from where they would be taken to the Portuguese embassy.
Some 15 special forces soldiers were already guarding the compound.
The Portuguese citizens would then cross the Zaire River to Brazzaville, Congo's capital, under the guard of the 68 troops.
Asked if Portuguese soldiers would respond if attacked, Lello said: "The soldiers are prepared for every eventuality. They will respond to the situation as they see fit."
Any decision to evacuate Portuguese nationals would follow a signal from the Portuguese ambassador in Kinshasa and final word from the defence and foreign ministries in Lisbon, Lello said.
He said the Portuguese planned to evacuate their own nationals but did not rule out that U.S. or other foreign troops could rescue some Portuguese citizens.
The United States rotated fresh Marines into Central Africa at the weekend and urged its nationals to leave Zaire.

The Marines arrived in Congo on Saturday to join French, Belgian and British troops on standby to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa in the event of a battle for the city or a rampage by Zaire's ragged and ill-disciplined army.
Several thousand Western nationals live in Zaire's capital, mainly citizens of France and the former colonial power, Belgium. The United States has 400 nationals there, Canada 500.
United Nations agencies stepped up security precautions in Kinshasa on Tuesday, evacuating a handful of non-essential staff.
